turns.learner: Hello! Can you give me an exercise on he, she and it with -s?
turns.tutor:
Here is the rule: after he, she or it, the verb takes -s (plays), -es (watches) or -ies (cries).
Right: "The robot washes the floor." Wrong: "The robot wash the floor." The robot is it, so the verb needs an ending.
My example: "The robot fixes cars." Fix ends in x, so I add -es.
Now you try. Write the verb:
Write the correct form: My sister ___ (play) tennis on Sundays. (answer with only the verb)
